children: Uncertainty over Indonesia's mining policy raises concerns about operating costs amid financial strain for miners, CreditSights analysts Jonathan Tan Jun Jie and Lakshmanan R say in a note. President Prabowo Subianto has proposed that at least 70% of proceeds generated under mining permits accrue to the state and suggested the government could take controlling stakes in mining companies, they note. How the 70% share would be calculated and implemented remains unclear, making the potential impact difficult to assess, they say. Meanwhile, Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia plans to impose a single-digit dollar-per-ton service fee on palm oil exports, with fees on coal and ferroalloys still undecided. These developments warrant a continued risk premium for the mining sector, they add. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
